sources.title: Primary architecture guidance
sources.content: Access decisions belong to the application boundary. A model instruction does not replace an authorization decision.

sources.title: Primary review guidance
sources.content: Consequential operations need an explicit review policy. Test failures as well as successful outcomes.

website.summary: A substantive mocked editorial fixture, never published content.
website.seoDescription: Understand practical permission boundaries and review decisions.

blocks.text: Start by defining which business operation the application is allowed to perform and who is responsible for it. The interface should make that boundary visible rather than assuming that a confident answer means an action is safe. Before adding another tool, inspect the information it receives, the permission it needs, and the confirmation a person should see. This example describes a design choice, not a report of a deployed customer system. Keep the existing reliable workflow available while checking how the new capability behaves when a dependency is unavailable. Document the tradeoff and review it with the operational owner.

linkedin.text: A confident answer is not an authorization decision. Before connecting an assistant to a business operation, define who can approve it and what happens when the tool fails. Start with one boundary you can explain to the person who owns the workflow.
linkedin.takeaway: Name the operation owner and the review boundary before adding a tool.
